newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX Hub natgas still up late on short covering.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX Hub natgas still up late on short covering.

text.p: NYMEX Henry Hub natgas futures remained higher late Tuesday in fairly active trade, with the complex still lifted by technical buying and short covering amid a steady physical market and revised weather forecasts.
At 1430 EDT, August was up by six cents at $2.128 per million British thermal units, while September was still 4.8 cents higher at $2.13. Others were up by by 0.9 to 3.5 cents.
"Cash values have been holding pretty well, and I think you have some nervous shorts out there. I think the new range is probably between $2.10 and $2.20 (basis August)," said one Texas-based trader.
Traders said attractive spreads between cash and futures and summer and winter months also contributed to the early buying spree.
In addition, revised forecasts today calling for some warmer eastern and West Coast temperatures next week helped keep the shorts uneasy.

Technical traders saw support in August at today's low of $2.051, with psychological support at $2. Resistance was now pegged at $2.15 and then along the down trendline at $2.25-2.26. Further selling was likely at the recent $2.36 high and then at the $2.415 contract high.
"We're looking at some broad based short covering today. The whole strip is moving up," a Midwest trader said, noting some buy stops were hit when August broke above $2.12.

In the cash Tuesday, Gulf Coast prices held steady at about $2.10. Midcon pipes were unchanged to up a penny in the high-$1.90s. New York city gate gas also was quoted little changed in the high-$2.30s.
Early injection estimates for Wednesday's AGA storage report range from 70 to 100 bcf versus a 90 bcf build last year.
NYMEX said 32,086 contracts traded at 1410 EDT.
On the KCBT, August was still up by 5.5 cents at $2.01, while deferreds were steady to 3.8 cents higher. The East/West spread widened by one-half cent to 11.8 cents (NYMEX premium).
